data.narrative: The student successfully decomposed the risk-ordered backlog into 5 end-to-end vertical slices. When confronted with stakeholder scope pressure to add Stripe payments prematurely, the student made a sound tradeoff decision by isolating Stripe integration into a standalone sandbox spike (Slice 1.5), preserving the main schedule while validating the core payment loop.

dimension_scores.observation: Extracted slice definitions that capture all functional layers (UI, Logic, DB) while strictly adhering to the ultra-thin constraints.
dimension_scores.evidence: Defined Slice 1 with an anonymous listing creation form and redirect without premature auth or calendar systems.

dimension_scores.observation: Constructed slices that build on each other logically, maintaining a sequential pipeline of capabilities.
dimension_scores.evidence: Mapped Slice 2 (onboarding vetting) to build on Slice 1, and Slice 3 (calendars) to build on Slice 2.

dimension_scores.observation: Demonstrated solid risk awareness by keeping the scariest novelty risks (payment integrations and calendars) isolated or stubbed.
dimension_scores.evidence: Acknowledged Stripe payment as an integration risk and isolated it using a stub contract signature and a separate spike.

dimension_scores.observation: Produced clear slice specifications with unambiguous boundaries, comprehensive anti-scopes, and human-testable acceptance criteria.
dimension_scores.evidence: Provided specific anti-scope listings (e.g., 'no admin auth', 'no notifications') and concrete step-by-step user confirmation flows.

dimension_scores.observation: Adapted efficiently to stakeholder scope pressure, immediately selecting a sandbox payments spike tradeoff instead of folding or starting over.
dimension_scores.evidence: Agreed to proceed with adding a sandbox payments spike (Slice 1.5) to keep the core profile demo on time.

dimension_scores.observation: Formulated a plan where all slices assemble into a unified platform, addressing the transition from mock stubs to live Stripe routing.
dimension_scores.evidence: Mapped out the final replacement of the payment stub with live Stripe redirects in Slice 5 after basic directory and auth structures are in place.

strengths: Demonstrated excellent scope management by defending the ultra-thin MVP boundary and using a separate sandbox payments spike to handle stakeholder scope pressure.
data.recommendation: Maintain this strong level of scope control when writing precise task specifications in Module 5.

public_evidence.student_action: Decomposed the project into 5 vertical slices and adapted the plan to include a payments sandbox spike.
public_evidence.technical_detail: Vertical slicing definition and adaptation plan for SkillSwap.
public_evidence.proof: artifacts/slices-module-04.md contains Slice 1.5 (Stripe Payments Sandbox Spike) and details scope, anti-scope, and acceptance criteria.
public_evidence.ability: Vertical slicing and scope management under stakeholder pressure.
public_evidence.reviewer_value: Shows the ability to partition a complex roadmap into testable deliverables and make balanced tradeoff decisions under deadline constraints.

concepts_demonstrated.evidence: Decomposed the SkillSwap requirements into top-to-bottom feature wedges.
Kept MVP boundary ultra-thin and handled investor demo constraint using a sandbox spike.

teaching_approaches.detail: Explained vertical vs. horizontal slices using a layer cake analogy and ASCII diagrams.
